headline: Census Confirms 60% of Meridian Residents Claim Mixed Heritage
body: The GLMZ Civic Census Office released its decadal population report this morning, confirming that 61.4% of the city's 14.2 million residents now self-identify as carrying heritage from two or more distinct ethnic or national lineages — the first time in the city's recorded history that mixed-heritage residents constitute a clear majority. The milestone is being attributed to four generations of dense urban migration into the megacity's core, compounded by the deliberate resettlement programs following the Great Lakes infrastructure collapse of the 2080s, which drew populations from across the former continental US, East Asia, West Africa, and South America into shared residential corridors. Cultural analysts at the independent Meridian Futures Institute note that the shift is reshaping naming conventions, culinary zones, spiritual practice, and even BCI interface language preferences across the city's districts. 'Meridian was never a melting pot — it was always a pressure cooker,' said demographer Kwame Johanssen-Cruz of the Institute. 'What you're seeing now is a population that has metabolized that pressure into something genuinely new.' The Federal Remnant's heritage classification board, which still maintains ethnic registry categories inherited from pre-collapse federal structures, has not commented on the census findings.
aftermath: The 2123 census became foundational evidence in The Wishing Well's 2126 philosophical manifesto 'The Unmarked Body,' which argued that Meridian's demographic reality had already made legacy identity categories obsolete — a document that reshaped cultural politics in the city for a decade.
runner_relevance: The census data itself became a commodity. Corponations — particularly Ringo's consumer analytics division and Helix Biosystems' demographic targeting arm — paid for granular, block-level breakdowns that the Civic Census Office withheld from public release. Runners were hired as data couriers and broker intermediaries, moving restricted demographic packages to buyers in The Spires. Conversely, community organizations in the Gray Zone hired runners to intercept or delay the same data transfers, fearing the information would be used to redraw residential zoning and displace existing communities.
